notes_for_us: Roughly three quarters of this prompt is UX ethics and monetisation policy. constraints could hold the non-negotiables, which is better than dropping them, but kind only offers fidelity, build_rule and reference and none of those is what a child-safety policy is. It went in as one long build_rule.

Simulation's own note says role sims are usually cooperative shared farms, and the Role Sim preset has no plot at all — but this prompt asks for both co-op play and 'each other's farms', which is per-player plots. The genre's guidance and the prompt's wording pull opposite ways on the decision the file itself calls the highest-cost one.

Visiting another player's farm is the one place the prompt touches the route, and the skill gives no rule for it: plots on one map is P0, separate places is P4, and nothing in the files says which reading a 'visit a friend's farm' game defaults to.

There is no option for animal husbandry stations — feeding troughs, brushing spots, egg collection — so all of it was folded into trigger-task, whose wording ('patient bed, planting plot') just about stretches. A prompt whose whole reward loop is animal care leans hard on one row.

The brief's 'take the whole preset' rule and the skill's 'never inject an option the user did not choose' collide head-on here: every no-genre preset adds geometry and the prompt forbids adding geometry.
